questions.solution:
**Given:**

Simplify: (3)/(2) times (11)/(5) div ((25)/(44) times (11)/(5)) div (33)/(15)

**Calculation:**

Step 1: Simplify the expression inside the parentheses:

(25)/(44) times (11)/(5) = (25 times 11)/(44 times 5) = (275)/(220) = (5)/(4)

Step 2: The expression now becomes:

(3)/(2) times (11)/(5) div (5)/(4) div (33)/(15)

Step 3: Simplify the division operations:

(11)/(5) div (5)/(4) = (11)/(5) times (4)/(5) = (44)/(25)

Step 4: The expression now becomes:

(3)/(2) times (44)/(25) div (33)/(15)

Step 5: Simplify the next division:

(44)/(25) div (33)/(15) = (44)/(25) times (15)/(33) = (44 times 15)/(25 times 33) = (660)/(825) = (4)/(5)

Step 6: Final multiplication:

(3)/(2) times (4)/(5) = (12)/(10) = (6)/(5)

**∴ The simplified value is (6)/(5).**

questions.question: The value of the expression 1800 ÷ 10{(18 - 6) + [-2(1 + 2 )]} is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the nested terms from inside out: (1 + 2) = 3 and (18 − 6) = 12.

The middle term becomes [−2 × 3] = −6.

The brace term becomes {12 + (−6)} = 6.

The expression reduces to 1800 ÷ 10{6}, which is 1800 ÷ 60.

Calculation: 1800 ÷ 60 = 30.

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: 1800 ÷ 10{(18 − 6) + [−2(1 + 2)]}

Formula: VBODMAS (Vinculum, Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 1800 ÷ 10{(12) + [−2(3)]}

⇒ 1800 ÷ 10{12 + (−6)}

⇒ 1800 ÷ 10{12 − 6}

⇒ 1800 ÷ 10{6}

⇒ 1800 ÷ (10 × 6)

⇒ 1800 ÷ 60

⇒ 30

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

It defines the sequence for solving mathematical operations: Vinculum → Brackets → Of → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction.

Bracket Priority

Always solve in the order of: circular brackets ( ), then curly braces { }, and finally square brackets [ ].

Implicit Multiplication

In many competitive exams, a number adjacent to a bracket (juxtaposition) is treated as a priority operation, similar to the Of (O) step.</p
